author: Codex / comp05 independent parti author
assumptions: Programme and required floor area are unknown. None of these alternatives certifies programme compliance.
Registered road-facing edges support a public-address question; precise entrances, access, survey datum, parking, cores and structure remain unverified.
The four propositions compare continuous enclosure, folded section, grounded radial wings and bearing stacked bars. Lower density is a tradeoff, never a merit by itself.

schemes.name: sangok_c05_inhabited_inclined_ring
schemes.secondary_language: One inhabited ring with a rising sectional edge
schemes.formal_principle: 하나의 넓은 중정을 감싸는 몸이 낮은 전면에서 높은 뒤쪽으로 이어지며 열린 하늘과 실내 깊이의 관계를 단면으로 만든다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: Continuous inhabited ring with one rising roof profile
schemes.reference_basis: Original authorship: provisional public-address hypothesis on the registered parcel; no prescribed rooms or required area supplied.

ops.why: A road-facing public address must coexist with interior depth; establish a four-storey maximum working volume, then organize it around a single sky opening. Actual programme remains unknown.

The need for a legible collective interior suggests one courtyard rather than separate garden pockets; a deep inhabited ring falls continuously from four-storey rear capacity to a two-storey edge. This makes enclosure and sectional asymmetry visible; roof access, actual upper floor layouts and entrance cuts are not established.

schemes.name: sangok_c05_folded_room_comb
schemes.secondary_language: Three deep room fingers tied by a common spine and folded section
schemes.formal_principle: 세 개의 깊은 실내 날개와 하나의 연결 몸이 두 외부 틈을 만들고 반복되는 접힌 단면이 각 날개의 공간적 크기를 드러낸다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: Room-depth comb with repeated folded roof sections
schemes.reference_basis: Original authorship: a provisional alternative to a deep undifferentiated public building, not a verified programme schedule.

ops.why: A public-office classification supplies no room schedule; test whether three substantial room fingers can give a deep building shorter edges to open air. Three storeys establish useful depth without claiming required area.

An undifferentiated deep plate gives no hierarchy to its interior; two full-depth external slots separate three occupied fingers while a broad rear spine keeps one building. A folded top aligns each ridge to one finger, making section follow organization; daylight performance, roof structure and rooms under sloping ceilings need later verification.

schemes.name: sangok_c05_radial_three_wings
schemes.secondary_language: Three grounded radial wings address a shared open centre
schemes.formal_principle: 서로 다른 크기의 세 날개가 열린 중심을 향해 돌아서며 하나의 기단 없이도 건물 사이의 접근과 독립성을 구성한다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: Three grounded wings turn toward a common centre
schemes.reference_basis: Original authorship: tests separated public-building wings as a spatial hypothesis; programme allocation and enclosed connections remain unknown.

ops.why: The parcel has several registered street edges, so a single front is only one possible address; place three substantial wings around an open centre with their own ground contact and differing sizes. This creates a multi-address ensemble rather than the previous flat-topped orthogonal pavilion grid; access rights, travel distances and room allocations remain unverified.

Separated wings need coherent occupied sections rather than unrelated rooftop ornaments; ridge each wing along its own local long axis, letting the rotated 4x4 placements carry its section with it. The resulting roof family unifies the ensemble without a connecting slab; roof structure and upper-level headroom require design.

schemes.name: sangok_c05_bearing_bar_assembly
schemes.secondary_language: Three levels of bearing bars with alternating modest rotation
schemes.formal_principle: 낮게 펼친 두 받침 몸 위로 긴 실내 몸들을 엇놓아 쌓아 지상 여유와 상부의 방향성을 하나의 입체적 집합으로 만든다.
schemes.dominant_gesture: Bearing bars alternate direction across three occupied levels
schemes.reference_basis: Original authorship: compact multi-level alternative for the same unquantified public-office brief; not a structural design or maximum-FAR target.

ops.why: The same parcel can reserve ground by placing occupied bars above a broader bearing base; distribute five one-storey bars over three levels and alternate their local rotation, with modest longitudinal displacement. The spatial proposition is the inhabited stacked assembly itself, not a block plus small appendages; support overlap, cores, egress and the usefulness of each floor remain to be tested, and no floor-area sufficiency is asserted.

schemes.name: loop_butterfly_open__d07_bar+
schemes.secondary_language: a four-storey loop ring whose every bar carries a butterfly roof draining toward the court - a basin of roofs over a garden of rain
schemes.formal_principle: The court is the ring's centre but a flat ring drains rain away from it; giving every bar a butterfly that drains toward the court makes the court a rain garden that the building actively feeds - the building is organised around its own hydrological logic, the butterfly valleys as gutters pointing inward.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a court ring of butterfly roofs draining to the court

ops.why: Input: a four-storey ring tall enough that the butterfly's valley is visible above the bar's eaves; height 0.65 declares mid-tall. Bar 0.23 gives each arm enough depth for a readable butterfly across its short dimension. Limit: four storeys keep the ring civic-scaled; bar 0.23 avoids making the arms too deep for the butterfly to register.

Input: the butterfly valley runs along each bar's cross axis (parallel to the court edge) so the valley is the deepest point closest to the court; at 0.3 biases the valley toward the court face so the deep wing is over the court and the shallow wing faces outward. Limit: pitch 0.55 on bar depth 0.23 reads cleanly within the cap; along cross runs the valley perpendicular to each bar's own length.

schemes.name: sangok_c04_develop_perforated_base
schemes.secondary_language: Perforated base beneath a continuous upper body
schemes.formal_principle: Lift a narrow transverse strip of the underside to form a covered ground passage through the central body and rear wall. The continuous upper volume frames the two carved courts while the retained north and south masses remain grounded.
schemes.dominant_gesture: Perforated base beneath a continuous upper body
schemes.reference_basis: Exact scored comp04 parent; architectural massing development. Public-office and meeting uses remain hypotheses.

ops.why: Retain the parent two-storey, 7.8 m maximum envelope and 3.9 m authored storey height.

design_argument_ko.title: Perforated base beneath a continuous upper body
design_argument_ko.spatial_strategy: Lift a narrow transverse strip of the underside to form a covered ground passage through the central body and rear wall. The continuous upper volume frames the two carved courts while the retained north and south masses remain grounded.
design_argument_ko.tradeoff: The passage is a modeled void, not a verified door, circulation route or engineered transfer structure. Its upper bridge needs structural development.
